chunks: Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the ghusl of Friday, so he said:

“It is obligatory in travel and residence, except that women have been given concession during travel due to scarcity of water. The ghusl of janābah is obligatory, and the ghusl of menstruation is obligatory, and the ghusl of the mustaḥāḍah is obligatory. If she inserts cotton and the blood passes beyond the cotton, then ghusl is upon her for every two prayers, and for Fajr there is a ghusl. But if the blood does not pass beyond the cotton, then wudu (ablution) is upon her for every salat (prayer). The ghusl of the woman in nifās is obligatory, and the ghusl of the newborn is obligatory, and the ghusl of the dead is obligatory, and the ghusl of one who has washed a dead person is obligatory, and the ghusl of the muḥrim is obligatory, and the ghusl of the day of ʿArafah is obligatory, and the ghusl of ziyārah is obligatory except for one who has an illness. And the ghusl for entering the House is obligatory, and the ghusl for entering the Ḥaram is obligatory, and it is recommended that a man not enter it except with ghusl. And the ghusl of mubāhalah is obligatory, and the ghusl of istisqāʾ is obligatory. And the ghusl of the first night of the month of Ramaḍān is recommended, and the ghusl of the night of the twenty-first is sunnah (prophetic tradition), and the ghusl of the night of the twenty-third—do not leave it, for it is hoped that Laylat al-Qadr is in one of those two nights. And the ghusl of the day of al-Fiṭr and the ghusl of the day of al-Aḍḥā—I do not like that they be left. And the ghusl of istikhārah is recommended.”

key_terms.الِاسْتِخَارَةِ: seeking divine guidance, for which ghusl is recommended
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton used to detect or absorb blood
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: a woman experiencing irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution) required for prayer in certain cases
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the obligatory ritual bath after janabah
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْمُحْرِمِ: the ritual bath associated with entering ihram
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree sought in the last nights of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Which types of ghusl are obligatory or recommended according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith lists a range of ritual baths, distinguishing those described as obligatory from those recommended or emphasized. It is a jurisprudential text on taharah (ritual purity), especially concerning women’s rulings, funerary matters, hajj-related acts, sacred-entry rites, and selected nights and days of worship.
